about.title: Orange Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails in your kitchen on Chapman Avenue, in a garage off Tustin Street, or in a car on SR-55 was supposed to work. When it doesn't and someone gets hurt, California law takes a practical view: you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. Under strict liability, what matters is whether the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and whether that defect caused your injury. Orange is home to about 141,000 people, and all of them rely on appliances, tools, vehicles, medications, and children's gear built somewhere else by companies they will never meet. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor, and the retailer that sold the item. Our team handles product liability cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Keep the product, keep the packaging, and reach out when you are ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Orange Residents Choose Us for Product Cases

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: California generally lets an injured person recover by showing the product was defective and caused the harm, without proving the company was negligent. We can evaluate whether your case fits a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.title: More than one company may owe you
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the store in Orange that sold the item can all share liability under California law. Our team can sort out which parties belong in the claim.

items.title: Guidance on preserving the evidence
items.desc: The product itself is usually the heart of a defect case, so it should not be thrown away, repaired, or returned. We advise on keeping it intact from the start.

items.question: My crash on SR-55 in Orange may have been caused by a part failure, not another driver. Is that a product case?
items.answer: It can be. Orange recorded 819 injury collisions in 2025, and while most involve driver error, some trace back to failed tires, brakes, steering components, or airbags that did not deploy. If a defective part contributed to your injuries, the manufacturer and sellers of that part may be liable under strict liability. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until we have reviewed it.

items.question: I no longer have the receipt for the product that hurt me. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Purchase records can often be recovered through bank statements, online order histories, or the store's own systems, and the product itself carries model and lot information that helps identify the maker. What matters most is preserving the item and documenting your injuries. Our team can help track down the rest.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Under California's strict liability approach, generally no. You typically need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings, that you used it in a reasonably foreseeable way, and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company knew or was careless is usually not the central question, though we will review the specifics of your situation.
